subject: Reservation drift + Dedicated GPU pool queueing — urgent customer coordination
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@honeypay.com>, Honeypay SRE <sre@honeypay.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Reservation drift + Dedicated GPU pool queueing — urgent customer coordination

Team / Olivia —

We’re seeing a sustained reservation drift for Honeypay’s dedicated GPU pool starting ~07:40 UTC. Key signals:
- Reserved throughput observed at the infra layer has fallen from the contracted baseline of ~1,200 qps to ~450 qps over the last 30m.
- Customer-side queue depth (per their dashboard & our prefix logs) is ~3x normal and still growing; screenshot attached.
- p95 latency has climbed to ~2.6s (baseline ~0.7s) and error rate (5xx) is at ~0.9% (baseline ~0.02%).

Attached: honeypay_qps_logs.txt (minute-level token and queueing traces), screenshot-queue-depth.png.

Immediate asks:
1) Irene / Infra: can you confirm whether autoscaler made unintended evictions or if allocation drift occurred across the dedicated pool? Check node assignments and reservation metadata for HP-3421.
2) Priyom / Oncall: please stage an emergency burst pool and stand up the soft-fallback routing for Honeypay (route <10% traffic to hosted-lowcost while we stabilize).
3) Marissa / CS: Olivia — can you confirm business impact in minutes lost or checkout failure rate? We need that for exec prioritization.
4) Vivek: If this will be >2 hours, please authorize customer-facing contingency credits and leader-level war room.

Proposed immediate mitigation (if infra agrees): 1) hot-push extra burst nodes to the dedicated PoP, 2) apply soft-eviction to lower-priority tenants sharing the same host, 3) promote Honeypay to the low-latency model variant while we reprovision.

I’ll open a war room bridge once infra confirms status.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@honeypay.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Honeypay SRE <sre@honeypay.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reservation drift + Dedicated GPU pool queueing — urgent customer coordination

Aditya —

Thanks for flagging. Confirming: our checkout checkout-api errors spiked at 07:42 UTC and we began to have intermittent timeouts. Impact: ~4% of checkouts are failing right now (rough estimate), time-to-confirm for transactions has more than doubled. This is visible on our side both in the user-facing flows and in our internal metrics.

We’ve attached the local traces to the SRE alias. Please treat as Sev-1 — our revenue window is open and this is customer-impacting. We appreciate a quick remediation path and we’re ready to join a bridge.

—Olivia
Olivia Chen
Head of Payments Operations, Honeypay
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@honeypay.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reservation drift + Dedicated GPU pool queueing — urgent customer coordination

Working this now — quick observations from the control plane:
- Reservation metadata shows hp-3421 still has a full commit, but agent heartbeats indicate two worker nodes went into maintenance state at 07:38 UTC (likely scheduled kube node upgrade that overlapped maintenance windows). Autoscaler removed replacement nodes but failed to rebind reserved capacity to the existing pool.
- Root cause candidate: node upgrade + a bug in the node-rebind logic that leaves reserved slots orphaned until manual reconciliation.

Immediate actions taken:
1) I requested manual rebind of reservation slots for HP-3421 (ticket SRV-789).
2) Priyom is prewarming 3 burst instances in the same region and will apply soft-eviction to best-effort tenants on the affected hosts.
3) Config to route 15% of Honeypay traffic to hosted-low-latency model variant (model: redwood-lt-v2) is staged and will be live in ~8-12 minutes.

If routing and burst nodes do not restore p95 < 1s within 20 minutes, we should flip to emergency dedicated reallocation (cold migration) which will require authorization from leadership due to cross-customer impact.

Attaching mutual_action_plan_v2.pdf (proposed step-by-step).

—Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Platform Reliability
irene_choi@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@honeypay.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Reservation drift + Dedicated GPU pool queueing — urgent customer coordination

Vivek — looping you in because this is likely to require cross-functional exec attention (customer revenue exposure, potential SLA credit).

Quick summary for execs: Honeypay (HP-3421) experienced a reservation drift that reduced their effective throughput by ~60% for ~90 minutes; customer-visible checkout failures reported. Irene’s team is running staged mitigations (burst nodes + soft routing). We need decision on:
- Approving emergency cross-customer eviction to rebind capacity now (risk: transient impact to other reserved customers).
- Approving one-time credit (I propose 10% monthly credit for impacted window) pending postmortem.

Please advise. If you prefer a short sync, I can set a 15-minute bridge now.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@honeypay.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reservation drift + Dedicated GPU pool queueing — urgent customer coordination

Update from ops (short):
- Applied manual rebind and prewarmed 3 burst instances at 08:55 UTC; soft-routing to redwood-lt-v2 went live at 09:10 UTC.
- Observed reductions in queue depth starting at 09:18 UTC; p95 back to ~0.95s by 09:35 UTC. Error rate falling toward baseline (now 0.06%).
- No global rebind/eviction was required; we avoided cold migrations.

Next steps:
1) Postmortem (owner: Irene) due EOD tomorrow — will include root cause, timeline, and mitigations (control plane fix + policy change to prevent node upgrades overlapping reserved maintenance windows).
2) Recommend adding a contractual burst buffer for HP-3421 (30% burst credit) and a runbook change to surface node-upgrade plans to account teams.
3) Customer-facing note: Marissa to send a short recap to Olivia with timelines, customer credits (pending Vivek), and an ask for any additional traces.

Thanks everyone — will stay on follow-up items.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Oncall Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
